themes_detail.label: Tree Damage Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Damaged tree complaints exploded to 7 THIS WEEK vs. 0.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks—a 1300% spike (z-score: 9.19)—suggesting either severe weather damage, infrastructure failure, or unaddressed maintenance across the district.
evidence: 7 damaged tree complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.5 weekly average (prior 8 weeks)
Highest z-score spike in entire dataset (9.19, severity: high)
Represents 1300% increase, most dramatic single-category anomaly
reporting_angles: Site visits to identify specific trees and assess public safety risk; interview Parks Department on response timeline
Investigate whether recent weather events (windstorms, heavy snow) or deferred maintenance drove the spike; compare to other NYC districts

themes_detail.label: Street Infrastructure Deterioration
themes_detail.summary: Street condition complaints surged to 75 THIS WEEK vs. 18.6 weekly average—a 303% spike (z-score: 8.75)—alongside parallel spikes in sidewalk (140% up), street sweeping (789% up), and root/sewer damage complaints, indicating systemic street infrastructure failure.
evidence: Street condition: 75 complaints THIS WEEK vs. 18.6 weekly average (303% increase, z-score: 8.75)
Sidewalk condition: 18 complaints LAST WEEK vs. 7.5 weekly average (140% increase, z-score: 4.7)
Street sweeping: 10 complaints LAST WEEK vs. 1.1 weekly average (789% increase, z-score: 4.52)
Root/sewer/sidewalk: 3 complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.5 weekly average (500% increase, z-score: 5.0)
CB budget repeatedly requests 'Repair or build new step streets' (DOT), signaling chronic unmet need
reporting_angles: Map 311 complaints geographically to identify hotspot neighborhoods; conduct ground reporting on specific blocks to document conditions
Interview DOT on deferred maintenance backlog and resource constraints; compare UES street investment to other districts

themes_detail.label: Street Lighting Failure Surge
themes_detail.summary: Street light condition complaints jumped to 32 LAST WEEK vs. 7.4 weekly average—a 334% spike (z-score: 7.79)—raising public safety concerns in a district with high evening foot traffic.
evidence: Street light complaints: 32 LAST WEEK vs. 7.4 weekly average (334% increase, z-score: 7.79)
Represents sustained surge over single week with no recent prior spikes in this category
Overlaps temporally with street infrastructure spike, suggesting possible cascading infrastructure failure
reporting_angles: File FOIL request for Con Edison street light maintenance/outage logs for past month; identify whether bulk failures occurred on specific date
Interview residents on safety perception; document which avenues/streets are darkest; report on response time from Con Ed

themes_detail.label: For-Hire Vehicle Complaints Rising
themes_detail.summary: For-hire vehicle complaints (Uber/Lyft-related) jumped to 19 LAST WEEK vs. 8.0 weekly average—a 138% spike (z-score: 3.72)—suggesting new parking, congestion, or behavior issues tied to platform economy growth.
evidence: For-hire vehicle complaints: 19 LAST WEEK vs. 8.0 weekly average (138% increase, z-score: 3.72)
Illegal parking remains chronic high-volume issue (1452 complaints over 90 days), UES demographic may be particularly affected by ride-share growth
Suggests acceleration of trend rather than baseline problem
reporting_angles: Interview residents on whether for-hire vehicles are double-parking, idling, or blocking hydrants/loading zones; solicit specific complaint types
Check TLC data on license plate violations and parking citations for Uber/Lyft in district; compare enforcement over past month

themes_detail.label: Maintenance & Facility Neglect
themes_detail.summary: Maintenance or facility complaints spiked to 12 THIS WEEK vs. 3.8 weekly average—a 220% increase (z-score: 3.71)—potentially indicating neglected public buildings or infrastructure across the district.
evidence: Maintenance/facility complaints: 12 THIS WEEK vs. 3.8 weekly average (220% increase, z-score: 3.71)
CB budget requests repeatedly fund 'Renovate interior building component (DOE)' and 'Renovate NYCHA community facilities' (HA), indicating chronic facility deferred maintenance
Timing aligns with broader infrastructure spike across trees, streets, lights this week
reporting_angles: Identify which facilities generated complaints (schools, community centers, NYCHA buildings); assess maintenance backlogs via 311 database
Interview Community Board on facility condition priorities; assess whether budget requests were denied in prior fiscal years
